---
title: "Prepare your submission"
subtitle: "Learn how to prepare your submission for the Methods Hub"
---

You have an interesting method or tutorial you want to submit to the Methods Hub? Follow this guiding checklist to see what you need for your submission. 

## 1. Check if your submission meets our criteria! 

On the Methods Hub, we want to provide access to open methods and tutorials relevant for the social sciences.

**Scope**

- [ ] The method or tutorial is relevant for the social sciences.
- [ ] The method or tutorial belongs to a relevant task of the [Methods Hub Tasks Taxonomy](https://methodshub.gesis.org/submit/taxonomy/). If it does not fit into our taxonomy, contact us at [methodshub@gesis.org](mailto:methodshub@gesis.org).
- [ ] Make sure to make explicit how your submission relates to the social sciences (e.g., use cases, example data, contextualizations)

**Openness**

- [ ] The method or tutorial is developed in an open-source programming language (e.g., Python or R).
- [ ] The method or tutorial is publicly accessible in a Git repository.
- [ ] For methods: the Git repository contains one and only one method.
- [ ] The method or tutorial is [published under an open license](https://opensource.guide/legal/#which-open-source-license-is-appropriate-for-my-project).


## 2. Check if you included all necessary files! 

The following files **must** be in your Git repository before you submit. Below are links to templates you should use. 

**The content file.** Your repository needs a file containing the content that is rendered on the Methods Hub page. It should follow our template structure. We have different templates for methods and tutorials (check below). 

**Files necessary for Binder environment.** Your repository contains all files needed to set up a [Binder environment](https://mybinder.readthedocs.io/en/latest/examples/sample_repos.html#managing-languages) for the Methods Hub: a file specifying the requirements and a postBuild file that installs Quarto. These configuration files can be at the root level or in a directory named `.binder` or `binder`. The Binder environment needs to build without errors.

**Other.** Further, you need to add a `LICENSE` file with an open license and a `CITATION.cff` file at the root level. Without a license, others are not legally allowed to reuse your code, and a citation file makes sure your work is properly credited when they do.

##### Checklist of required files and templates
| File | Resource | Purpose | Template | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| README | Method | Contains content | [README template](https://github.com/YOUR-ORG/YOUR-REPO/blob/main/method/template.md?plain=1) | |
| Tutorial file | Tutorial | Contains content | [`template.qmd`](https://github.com/YOUR-ORG/YOUR-REPO/blob/main/tutorial/template.qmd) or [`template.ipynb`](https://github.com/YOUR-ORG/YOUR-REPO/blob/main/tutorial/template.ipynb) | Also possible: R Markdown, Pandoc Markdown |
| Requirements | Both | Reproducibility | Python: [`requirements.txt`](https://github.com/YOUR-ORG/YOUR-REPO/blob/main/binder-examples/python/requirements.txt); R: [`install.R`](https://github.com/YOUR-ORG/YOUR-REPO/blob/main/binder-examples/r/install.R); conda: [`environment.yml`](https://github.com/YOUR-ORG/YOUR-REPO/blob/main/binder-examples/conda/environment.yml) | Pin dependency versions; root level or in a directory named `.binder` or `binder` |
| postBuild | Both | Build process that installs Quarto | [`postBuild`](https://methodshub.gesis.org/snippet/postBuild) |root level or in a directory named `.binder` or `binder` |
| License | Both | Open license | [`LICENSE`](https://docs.github.com/en/communities/setting-up-your-project-for-healthy-contributions/adding-a-license-to-a-repository) | add at the root level |
| Citation file | Both | Citation | [`CITATION.cff`](https://citation-file-format.github.io/) | add at the root level |


## 3. Check how much you considered the readers of your submission!

The people using your method or tutorial will often be less familiar with it than you are. After all, you know the method inside out, while they may be seeing it for the first time. The easier it is to understand, run, and adapt, the more people will use it, and the more it will be cited.

Before submitting, check that:

**Readers can follow it**

- [ ] The code is commented, including the reasons behind key decisions, not just what each step does.
- [ ] Parameters are documented, so others know what they can change and what effect it has.
- [ ] Longer code is structured into modules or clearly separated sections.
- [ ] Text and comments are proofread for spelling, grammar, and clarity.

**Readers can run it in our interactive environments**

- [ ] Your submission runs in an interactive environment. Check it in the [Interactive Test Area](https://methodshub.gesis.org/submit/test-area).
- [ ] Set random seeds wherever randomness is involved.
- [ ] Report software and package versions (e.g., `sessionInfo()` in R or `pip freeze` in Python).
- [ ] Document where data comes from and under which license it can be reused.

Want more ideas? See our [documentation recommendations](criteria.qmd#documentation-quality).

You can suggest further venues by email to the [Methods Hub team](mailto:methodshub@gesis.org).

Want some more ideas? Check [our recommendations](criteria.qmd#documentation-quality)
